newsitem.title: USA: Independence Day top movie in People's Choice Awards.
newsitem.headline: Independence Day top movie in People's Choice Awards.

text.p: "Independence Day" won best film and Mel Gibson was named best actor on Sunday night in the 23rd annual People's Choice Awards, a fans' popularity contest for film, television and music.
Sandra Bullock was named best movie actress, and "Seinfeld" and "ER" were best television shows, all for the second straight year.
Three other winners took home the top prize for a second time while Bill Cosby and Michael J. Fox tied for favourite male performer in a new television series.
"At least it's not a half of one," Cosby said as he accepted his statue.
"Thanks Mom," Fox quipped to award presenter Lea Thompson who played his mother in the "Back to the Future" movies.

The awards show also featured a special tribute to actor-director Rob Reiner, with highlights from his days on TV's "All in the Family" and movies that he has acted in or directed such as "Sleepless in Seattle", "A Few Good Men" and "Ghosts of Mississippi".
Carl Reiner said of his son before presenting him with his award: "He's a wonderful guy, I know that, and that is more important than anything he can do in this business."
Reba McEntire accepted her award for favourite female musical performer on crutches, saying she injured herself in a skiing accident.

The awards were chosen by a nationwide telephone poll of Americans age 12 and above. Addressing the televised ceremony, George Gallup Jr., co-chair of the Gallup Organisation which conducted the poll, did not give an exact number of people surveyed, but said his group called thousands who represent 204 million Americans.
This year there was a new category for daytime television. The awards programme was hosted by Don Johnson and Roma Downey.
The winners were:
Motion Picture: Independence Day
Motion Picture Actress: Sandra Bullock (won for second year)
Motion Picture Actor: Mel Gibson
Comedy Motion Picture: The Nutty Professor
Female Television Performer: Oprah Winfrey
Male Television Performer: Tim Allen (won for second year)
Female Television Performer in a New Series: Brooke Shields
Male Television Performer in a New Series: Tie, Bill Cosby and Michael J. Fox
New Television Drama: Millennium
New Television Comedy: Cosby
Television Comedy Series: Seinfeld (won for second year)
Television Dramatic Series: ER (won for second year)
Daytime Serial: Days of Our Lives
Male Musical Performer: Garth Brooks (won for second year)
Female Musical Performer: Reba McEntire (won for second year)
